displayContract.byline: Assessments made by 5.6 Sol. — Rubric: Slugfester Reassessment Rubric v2.

thesis.text: The AI steelman is that theism offers a comparatively unified explanation of objective moral truth, categorical authority, equal personal worth, and defeasible moral knowledge when these are grounded in a necessarily good personal reality rather than contingent human endorsement.

novelty.explanation: This formulation repairs the live case by making its conclusion comparative and by distinguishing explanatory unification from a bare definitional assertion.

premises.text: If moral obligations are categorical, their authority cannot depend entirely on whether each affected person happens to endorse welfare, reciprocity, cooperation, or any other contingent goal.

novelty.explanation: This extends the transcript's dissenter challenge while carefully targeting endorsement-dependent authority rather than denying every secular reason.

premises.text: A necessarily good personal ground could unite moral standards with legitimate authority if goodness is substantively constitutive of that nature and creation establishes responsibility without reducing goodness to power.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the goodness-authority gap by separating divine power, substantive goodness, and responsibility instead of treating creation alone as sufficient.

premises.text: Equal human worth follows more securely if every person bears the same fundamental relation to a good creator, irrespective of popularity, ability, contribution, reciprocity, or present social valuation.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the compressed rights inference by identifying equal creator-relation as the proposed basis for status across unequal relationships.

premises.text: Theistic moral cognition need only be defeasibly reliable: divinely grounded capacities may remain fallible while evidence, reflection, experience, and interpersonal criticism correct particular judgments.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the epistemic account by incorporating the strongest secular correction method rather than presenting divine direction as automatic accuracy.

conclusion.text: Therefore, if these substantive claims about necessary goodness, legitimate creator-responsibility, equal status, and defeasible reliability are independently supported, theism would provide a more unified foundation for categorical ethics than endorsement-dependent secular alternatives.

novelty.explanation: The conclusion repairs overstatement by remaining conditional upon independent support for each disputed bridge and claiming comparative unification only.

newArguments.title: Invariant status under relational loss
newArguments.text: A foundation should protect persons precisely when ordinary sources of relational value collapse. An individual may become isolated, hated, unconscious, severely disabled, or unable to reciprocate, yet moral protection should not diminish with social attachment or expected contribution. A shared creator-relation offers an invariant status condition: relationships can enrich the reasons for care without creating the person's basic standing. This does not independently prove theism, but it supplies a comparative test that a secular relational account must meet with equally stable protections.

novelty.explanation: This is a new comparative stress test focused on whether moral status remains invariant when relationships, reciprocity, and contribution disappear.

newArguments.title: Authority and accountability convergence
newArguments.text: Ethical foundations are stronger when standards, authority, and accountability converge without becoming identical. On the steelmanned view, necessary goodness determines the standard, personal creation establishes a morally significant relationship, and accountability answers the practical question of why obligations concern particular agents. Each element still requires defense, but separating them avoids deriving goodness from power or authority from definition. The resulting structure also clarifies what evidence would count against the account: incoherence among divine character, purported commands, and equal personal worth.

novelty.explanation: This develops a three-part structure that directly repairs the conflation of power, goodness, authority, and accountability exposed during the exchange.

thesis.text: The AI steelman is that secular humanism can ground action-guiding ethics in impartial reasons arising from sentient vulnerability, agency, reciprocity, and shared social conditions while using public, fallible methods to correct judgments without positing divine authority.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the live case by presenting several convergent reason-giving bases rather than making moral authority depend upon one voluntarily selected goal.

premises.text: Sentient beings have standpoint-independent reasons to avoid severe suffering, coercion, and destroyed agency because those conditions frustrate interests that exist whether or not an aggressor endorses them.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the dissenter problem by locating reasons in affected interests rather than making obligation depend on the aggressor's chosen objective.

premises.text: Impartiality requires comparable interests to receive comparable consideration, preventing personal rejection of flourishing from erasing the claims of everyone exposed to that person's choices.

novelty.explanation: This introduces an impartiality principle that was not explicitly developed in the locked moves and directly addresses arbitrary exclusion.

premises.text: Reciprocity strengthens but does not create basic standing: social benefits generate additional duties, while vulnerability and agency protect persons unable to contribute or participate reciprocally.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the reciprocity bridge by preventing moral status from depending upon voluntary participation, contribution, or received social advantage.

premises.text: Public evidence, consistency testing, testimony, due process, and revision provide accountable methods for applying these standards, even though no method eliminates moral error or disagreement.

novelty.explanation: This extends the transcript's corrective method by integrating evidential inquiry with procedural safeguards and explicit epistemic modesty.

conclusion.text: Therefore, secular humanism can provide non-arbitrary moral reasons and publicly revisable guidance if it defends impartial consideration of vulnerability and agency, rather than treating well-being as merely an optional collective preference.

novelty.explanation: The conclusion repairs the conditionality weakness by grounding the case in affected interests and impartiality while keeping the claim proportionate.

newArguments.title: Reasons indexed to affected interests
newArguments.text: A dissenter's refusal to value welfare need not erase moral reasons, because reasons can be indexed to everyone affected rather than only to the acting person's preferences. Severe injury frustrates another person's agency, projects, relationships, and capacity for experience; those losses remain real facts about that person's standpoint. Impartial deliberation asks whether comparable interests are treated comparably across persons. The dissenter may remain unmoved, but motivational resistance no more cancels those reasons than disbelief about physical consequences cancels the consequences themselves.

novelty.explanation: This introduces an affected-interest account that separates the existence of reasons from an agent's endorsement or motivational responsiveness.

newArguments.title: Public corrigibility as comparative strength
newArguments.text: A moral framework gains practical authority when its applications can be challenged through reasons accessible to differently situated people. Evidence about harm, testimony from affected communities, consistency across similar cases, transparent procedures, and reversible policies create multiple opportunities for correction. This does not transform methodology into metaphysical proof, but it establishes a comparative advantage over disputed commands whose interpretation depends on inaccessible revelation or contested authority. Secular humanism can therefore claim institutional reliability modestly, while leaving deeper metaethical questions open to continued argument.

novelty.explanation: This extends the revisability and authority-gap moves into a comparative argument about publicly accessible correction and institutional reliability.
